title: Launch and inspect an EC2 instance

screens.title: Find EC2 and check the Region
screens.path: Console Home → Services → EC2 → Instances
screens.action: Select an approved Region, open Instances, then Launch instances.
screens.why: The Region and account define where the resource is created.

screens.title: Choose image and size
screens.path: Launch an instance → Name and tags → Application and OS Images → Instance type
screens.action: Name architect-console-lab; select Amazon Linux 2023 and an available small type.
screens.why: The AMI sets the OS; instance type sets compute and price.

screens.title: Configure login and network
screens.path: Launch an instance → Key pair (login) → Network settings → Edit
screens.action: Select or create a lab key; choose a VPC/public subnet, public IP, and SSH from My IP.
screens.why: A public address alone does not make SSH reachable. Routes, security group and credentials matter.
rows: Public subnet with internet gateway route

screens.title: Review storage and launch
screens.path: Launch an instance → Configure storage → Summary → Launch instance
screens.action: Check gp3 root volume and delete on termination, then review Summary and launch.
screens.why: Review access, networking, encryption, storage and estimated charges before committing.

screens.title: Verify, connect and clean up
screens.path: EC2 → Instances → Details / Security / Storage / Monitoring → Connect
screens.action: Confirm running and 2/2 checks; inspect addresses and security, connect, then terminate and verify residual resources.
screens.why: Running is not end-to-end health. Termination may leave separately created resources.
rows: Terminate; review volumes, key pair, IPs

title: Create a service role and inspect permissions

screens.title: Open Roles
screens.path: Console Home → IAM → Access management → Roles
screens.action: Choose Create role and inspect existing roles first.
screens.why: IAM is account-wide; roles are assumed identities.

screens.title: Select trusted entity
screens.path: Create role → Select trusted entity
screens.action: Choose AWS service and EC2 use case for a workload role.
screens.why: Trust policy controls who may assume the role.

screens.title: Add scoped permissions
screens.path: Create role → Add permissions
screens.action: Choose a narrowly scoped policy for a lab S3 read example; review its actions and resources.
screens.why: Permission policy determines what the role may do after assumption.

screens.title: Name and verify
screens.path: Create role → Name, review, and create → Role details
screens.action: Name the role, inspect trust and permissions tabs, then remove the lab role after use.
screens.why: A policy attachment is not proof the trust path or resource policy allows access.
rows: Detach lab policy and delete role

title: Build and trace a public subnet

screens.title: Create the VPC
screens.path: VPC → Your VPCs → Create VPC
screens.action: Choose VPC only, name lab-vpc, and select a non-overlapping IPv4 CIDR.
screens.why: CIDR overlap limits future connectivity.

screens.title: Create a subnet
screens.path: VPC → Subnets → Create subnet
screens.action: Choose lab-vpc, one Availability Zone and 10.20.1.0/24.
screens.why: Subnets live in one Availability Zone and inherit VPC address space.

screens.title: Attach gateway and route
screens.path: VPC → Internet gateways → Create / Attach → Route tables → Edit routes
screens.action: Attach an internet gateway and add 0.0.0.0/0 to it in a dedicated route table.
screens.why: A subnet becomes public by its effective route to an internet gateway.

screens.title: Associate and verify
screens.path: Route tables → Subnet associations → Edit associations
screens.action: Associate the lab subnet; inspect effective routes and security controls, then remove lab resources in dependency order.
screens.why: Creating a route table is insufficient until the subnet uses it.

title: Create and secure an S3 bucket

screens.title: Open bucket creation
screens.path: S3 → General purpose buckets → Create bucket
screens.action: Choose a globally unique lab bucket name and an approved Region.
screens.why: Bucket identity and Region affect naming and data location.

screens.title: Keep public access blocked
screens.path: Create bucket → Object Ownership → Block Public Access
screens.action: Keep bucket owner enforced and all Block Public Access settings enabled.
screens.why: A private lab bucket needs no public ACL or policy.

screens.title: Choose protection settings
screens.path: Create bucket → Bucket Versioning → Default encryption
screens.action: Enable versioning for this exercise; review default SSE-S3 encryption.
screens.why: Versioning helps recover prior versions; encryption and lifecycle are separate controls.

screens.title: Inspect and clean up
screens.path: Bucket → Objects / Properties / Permissions / Management
screens.action: Upload a harmless test file; inspect version ID and access; delete object versions, then bucket.
screens.why: Versioned buckets must be emptied of all versions and delete markers before deletion.

screens.title: Choose database engine
screens.path: RDS → Databases → Create database
screens.action: Select Standard create and an approved engine/version for a disposable lab.
screens.why: Standard create exposes networking, storage, backup and availability choices.

screens.title: Set instance and credentials
screens.path: Create database → Settings / Instance configuration / Storage
screens.action: Name the DB, select a small class and storage, and use approved credential management.
screens.why: Class and storage influence capacity and cost; never put real passwords into a training site.

screens.title: Set private connectivity
screens.path: Create database → Connectivity / Additional configuration
screens.action: Choose VPC, DB subnet group, public access No, and a narrow application security group.
screens.why: A private DB needs app-to-DB reachability, not public exposure.
rows: Allow app SG on DB port

screens.title: Inspect and delete
screens.path: RDS → Databases → Connectivity & security / Monitoring / Maintenance
screens.action: Inspect endpoint, port, backup and metrics; delete the disposable DB and review final snapshot choice.
screens.why: Database deletion and snapshots have lasting data and cost consequences.

title: Create and observe a Lambda function

screens.title: Create from scratch
screens.path: Lambda → Functions → Create function
screens.action: Choose Author from scratch, name the function, and select a supported runtime.
screens.why: Runtime, architecture and execution role govern compatibility and permissions.

screens.title: Review execution role
screens.path: Create function → Change default execution role
screens.action: Use a lab role with basic log permissions and inspect its IAM policy.
screens.why: The execution role is the function's AWS identity, distinct from who invokes it.

screens.title: Deploy and test
screens.path: Function → Code → Deploy → Test
screens.action: Deploy a simple handler, create a harmless test event and invoke once.
screens.why: A successful deployment does not prove an invocation succeeds.

screens.title: Inspect evidence and clean up
screens.path: Function → Monitor → View CloudWatch logs / Configuration
screens.action: Inspect result, duration, errors and logs; delete function and lab log group/role if appropriate.
screens.why: Logs and roles can remain after a function is deleted.

title: Inspect a metric and create an alarm

screens.title: Find the metric
screens.path: CloudWatch → Metrics → All metrics
screens.action: Choose the namespace, dimensions and metric for a lab resource.
screens.why: Metric dimensions identify the exact resource being monitored.

screens.title: Define alarm conditions
screens.path: Metrics → Graphed metrics → Create alarm
screens.action: Review period, statistic, threshold and missing-data treatment.
screens.why: A threshold without a period or missing-data policy is ambiguous.

screens.title: Choose actions
screens.path: Create alarm → Notification / Name and description
screens.action: Choose an approved SNS topic or no action for practice; name the alarm.
screens.why: Alarm evaluation and notification delivery are separate.

screens.title: Inspect state and cleanup
screens.path: CloudWatch → Alarms → All alarms → Alarm details
screens.action: Inspect history, state and graph; delete the lab alarm, and unsubscribe lab notifications if created.
screens.why: An OK state may reflect no recent breach, not necessarily that collection is healthy.

title: Trace a DNS record to its target

screens.title: Find hosted zone
screens.path: Route 53 → Hosted zones
screens.action: Open an existing authorized lab hosted zone; do not register a new domain for this exercise.
screens.why: A hosted zone is the authoritative DNS record container when delegation is correct.

screens.title: Create record
screens.path: Hosted zone → Create record
screens.action: Use a lab name, A/alias or CNAME as appropriate, and a controlled target.
screens.why: Alias choice and target type depend on the AWS resource.

screens.title: Review routing
screens.path: Create record → Routing policy / Evaluate target health
screens.action: Use Simple routing for a single target and review TTL/health options.
screens.why: Routing policy changes how clients receive answers.

screens.title: Test and cleanup
screens.path: Hosted zone → Test record / Records
screens.action: Test expected answer and inspect target health; remove only the lab record.
screens.why: A record can exist without public delegation or a healthy target.
